target.name: Validate sequential Docker restarts on staging hosts
target.description:
## Problem

In the infrastructure repository, `playbooks/deploy-app.yml` wrote `/etc/docker/daemon.json` and notified the `Restart Docker` handler without a `serial` or `throttle` setting.

A staging `deploy-app --check --diff` run with release `r-2026-10` showed a `daemon.json` change on all five staging hosts. The handler would have restarted Docker on all five hosts in one step, including the three storage hosts. Each storage host runs one ledger database node and one key-value store process.

The staging group `app_staging_all` also included host 9, which did not exist at the time of that run. The deploy tool locks every play host over SSH before the first task. The lock failed on host 9.

## Change

Infrastructure pull request 42 merged with the handler correction.

The new play, “Restart Docker one host at a time,” uses `serial: 1` and `any_errors_fatal: true`. It restarts Docker on hosts where `daemon.json` changed, or on every host when the run passes `docker_rolling_restart=true`. After each restart, it waits for the compose services that ran before the restart to become healthy. On each storage host, it also runs `ops ledger node-wait`.

The temporary inventory exclusion addressed host 9 before its creation. Host 9 now exists and runs the search engine.

## QA evidence

The deploy tool ran `deploy deploy-app --limit app_qa_all` with release `r-2026-10` and `docker_rolling_restart=true`. It acquired one host lock for six hosts. All six QA hosts finished with `failed=0` and `unreachable=0`.

Docker started again on each host one at a time. All times below use the local time zone of the QA site.

| Host | Docker start time |
| --- | --- |
| `qa-app1` | 21:16:59 |
| `qa-search1` | 21:18:28 |
| `qa-store1` | 21:19:38 |
| `qa-store2` | 21:21:31 |
| `qa-store3` | 21:23:13 |
| `qa-app2` | 21:24:37 |

The service health wait returned `ok` on every host. The ledger node wait returned `ok` on `qa-store1`, `qa-store2`, and `qa-store3`.

After the run, the ledger and store services reported healthy on all three storage hosts. The app on `qa-app1` answered `/healthz` with HTTP 200.

`ops search verify` on `qa-app1` reported `excluded_nodes` 0 and `stuck_work_items` 0.

No host retained a `deploy.lock` file. The controller had no remaining deploy tool or ansible-playbook process.

## Acceptance

1. The first staging deploy with release `r-2026-10` restarts Docker on the five staging hosts one at a time. The ledger node wait passes on each storage host before the next restart.
2. After that run, the staging app answers `/healthz`, and the ledger and store report healthy on all three storage hosts.

## Staging evidence and ownership

The deployment completed on the five staging hosts with failed=0. Docker restarted store1, app1, store2, store3, and app2 sequentially. The staging app and the three storage hosts currently report healthy services on release `r-2026-10`. This issue remains Done.

The deployment team owns this issue.

[Infrastructure pull request 42](https://example.com/infrastructure/pull/42) contains the handler correction. A separate issue handles the remaining generic absent-host behavior.

distractors.name: Merge Dependabot pull requests after required checks pass
distractors.description:
## Problem

Dependabot opens one pull request for each dependency update. A person approves and merges each one after CI passes. The queue grows by several pull requests each week.

## Change

Add `.github/workflows/dependabot-auto-merge.yml`. The workflow runs on `pull_request_target` for pull requests from `dependabot[bot]`. It reads the update type with `dependabot/fetch-metadata` and enables auto-merge for patch and minor updates. The repository ruleset still requires every status check before the merge.

## Acceptance

1. GitHub merges a Dependabot patch update after the required checks pass, without a manual approval.
2. GitHub leaves a major update open for review.
3. A failed check blocks the merge.

distractors.name: Set a stop grace period for the OpenSearch container
distractors.description:
## Problem

`docker compose stop` sends SIGTERM to the `opensearch` service and sends SIGKILL after the default ten seconds. OpenSearch needs longer than ten seconds to flush translogs and close shards on the search guest. A killed node replays its translog on the next start and reports yellow health for several minutes.

## Change

Set `stop_grace_period: 120s` on the `opensearch` service in `docker-compose.yml`. Keep the default for the other services.

## Acceptance

1. `docker compose stop opensearch` on QA finishes without SIGKILL.
2. The next start reports green health without a translog replay.

distractors.name: Restart the audit consumer when Kafka is down at startup
distractors.description:
## Problem

The `audit-consumer` container exits when it cannot connect to the Kafka broker during startup. Its compose restart policy is `on-failure:3`. Docker stops restarting the container after three failed attempts. A broker that starts slowly after a host reboot leaves the audit ledger without a writer.

## Change

The consumer waits for the broker with bounded backoff instead of exiting. The compose restart policy changes to `unless-stopped`.

## Acceptance

1. Stop the broker, start the consumer, then start the broker. The consumer connects and drains the outbox without a manual restart.
2. The consumer logs `audit.consumer.broker_wait` once per backoff step.

distractors.name: Recreate the app container after an image tag change
distractors.description:
## Problem

`docker compose up -d` recreated the `app` service only when its configuration changed. A deploy that changed `TACK_IMAGE_TAG` while Docker still cached the old image sometimes left the old container running.

## Change

The deploy runs `docker compose pull` before `docker compose up -d --force-recreate app audit-consumer`. `./server ops deploy verify` compares the running image digest with the digest that the deploy named.

## Acceptance

1. A deploy with a new tag replaces the `app` and `audit-consumer` containers.
2. `ops deploy verify` fails when a container runs a different digest.

distractors.name: Keep container IPv6 addresses after a Docker daemon restart
distractors.description:
## Problem

After `systemctl restart docker` on `tack-data2`, the `fdb` container received a new IPv6 address from the routed bridge. The NDP proxy still announced the old address. Peers could not connect to the store process until the proxy entry expired.

## Change

The compose file pins each service address with `ipv6_address` inside `TACK_DOCKER_V6_SUBNET`. The deploy renders the NDP proxy entries from the same values.

## Acceptance

1. A daemon restart keeps every service address.
2. `fdbcli --exec status` reports every process as available within one minute after the restart.

distractors.name: Wait for FoundationDB health before the app starts
distractors.description:
## Problem

The `app` service started before the `fdb` service accepted transactions. The first requests failed with `transaction_timed_out`. The readiness probe reported healthy because it checked only the HTTP listener.

## Change

Add `depends_on` with `condition: service_healthy` for `fdb` and `yugabyte`. The `/healthz` handler pings FoundationDB and YugabyteDB.

## Acceptance

1. `/healthz` returns HTTP 503 until both stores answer.
2. A cold boot on QA serves the first MCP request without a store error.

distractors.name: Run pending migrations before the app and consumer start
distractors.description:
## Problem

An audit-consumer image that expected migration 011 started on a host where the ledger was still at migration 010. The consumer failed every insert until an operator ran `./server migrate` by hand.

## Change

The full deploy runs `ops provision --execute` before it starts the `app` and `audit-consumer` services. Provision applies pending migrations in order and records each step through the ops audit choke point.

## Acceptance

1. A fresh QA host applies the latest migration before the consumer starts.
2. Provision records zero migration steps on a host that already has the latest migration.

distractors.name: Remove a stale deploy lock after an interrupted run
distractors.description:
## Problem

An interrupted `configsctl deploy` left `/var/lib/configsctl/deploy.lock` on `tack-app2`. The next deploy refused to start and reported that another run held the lock.

## Change

The lock file records the controller host, process ID, and run ID. `configsctl lock inspect` prints the lock owner. `configsctl lock release --run <id>` removes the lock only after the recorded process exits.

## Acceptance

1. `lock inspect` identifies the lock from an interrupted run.
2. `lock release` refuses to remove the lock of a live process.

distractors.name: Measure OpenSearch heap use during bulk indexing
distractors.description:
## Problem

The search guest reported circuit breaker rejections during a full replacement. The JVM heap rose to 92 percent while the worker sent bulk requests of 5 MiB.

## Change

Add a heap sampler that records `jvm.mem.heap_used_percent` every second during the native workload test. The test fails when the sample stays above 85 percent for ten consecutive seconds.

## Acceptance

1. The sampler records one value per second for the whole replacement.
2. The test report lists the peak heap, the time of the peak, and the bulk size at that time.

distractors.name: Rotate the audit signing key on QA
distractors.description:
## Problem

The QA audit signing key at `/etc/tack/audit-signing.pem` dates from the first QA build and has never changed. The compliance plan requires a tested rotation procedure before production rotation.

## Change

Generate a new Ed25519 key on `tack-qa`, add its identifier to `AUDIT_VALID_SIGNERS`, and deploy. Remove the old identifier after the export of every notarization signed with it.

## Acceptance

1. `audit signers` prints the new identifier as `local_signer`.
2. `audit export` verifies rows signed with both keys during the overlap.

distractors.name: Back up FoundationDB continuously to the object store
distractors.description:
## Problem

The product store had only nightly snapshots. A corruption found in the afternoon would lose every write since the previous night.

## Change

`ops provision` starts a continuous `fdbbackup` session that writes to the SeaweedFS bucket. The `fdb-backup-agent` service in the backup profile drains the session. The staleness check mails an alarm when the restorable version falls more than 15 minutes behind.

## Acceptance

1. The restore drill restores a point in time within the last 15 minutes.
2. A stopped backup agent produces one alarm mail.

distractors.name: Fix the restore drill when the scratch volume is full
distractors.description:
## Problem

The restore drill copied the ledger export into a scratch volume that still stored the files of the previous drill. The copy failed with `no space left on device`, and the drill reported a misleading checksum mismatch.

## Change

The drill removes its own scratch files from the previous run before it starts and checks free space against the export size. A full volume fails with an explicit space error.

## Acceptance

1. A drill after a failed drill succeeds without manual cleanup.
2. A volume smaller than the export fails before the copy with the required and available byte counts.

distractors.name: Bound the YugabyteDB health probe with a deadline
distractors.description:
## Problem

The ledger health check opened a connection with the default timeout. A silent node stalled each probe for two minutes, and the compose health check reported the container as starting for the whole period.

## Change

The probe connects with a five second deadline and runs `SELECT 1` with a two second statement timeout.

## Acceptance

1. A paused node reports unhealthy within ten seconds.
2. A healthy node answers the probe in under one second.

distractors.name: Exclude absent guests from deployment locks
distractors.description:
## Problem

configsctl locks every host in the play before the first task. A guest in the inventory that Proxmox does not have yet fails the lock, and the whole deployment stops.

## Change

configsctl compares the inventory with the Proxmox node and VMID list before it locks hosts. configsctl removes a confirmed absent, unenrolled guest from both the lock set and the deployment selection. An unreadable inventory or a missing enrolled guest fails the run.

## Acceptance

1. A deployment with one absent unenrolled guest locks and deploys the remaining guests.
2. A missing enrolled guest fails the run before any lock.

distractors.name: Pin the OpenSearch model bundle digest
distractors.description:
## Problem

The search guest downloaded the sparse model from the public model repository on first start. A changed upstream bundle could change every embedding without a mapping change.

## Change

`ops search provision` verifies the bundle SHA-256 and the tokenizer SHA-256 before it registers the model. The index mapping records the model ID and tokenizer digest.

## Acceptance

1. A bundle with a different digest fails provisioning.
2. `ops search verify` reports the mapping model and tokenizer identities.

distractors.name: Measure search latency under mixed read and write load
distractors.description:
## Problem

Search acceptance measured query latency only on an idle index. Production runs indexing and queries at the same time.

## Change

`ops qa datagen search-mixed` sends public search requests at a fixed offered rate while it writes nodes through MCP. The report separates offered, sent, completed, dropped, and failed requests and records p50, p95, and p99 latency.

## Acceptance

1. The report lists every request category and latency percentile.
2. The run records freshness for every written node.

distractors.name: Compose services report unhealthy after a guest reboot
distractors.description:
## Problem

After a Proxmox host reboot, `tack-data3` started all compose services at once. YugabyteDB and FoundationDB competed for disk during recovery, and both health checks failed for six minutes. The deploy health gate timed out.

## Change

Increase the health check `start_period` for `yugabyte` and `fdb` to five minutes. The deploy health gate waits up to ten minutes and prints the last health output for each service.

## Acceptance

1. After a guest reboot on QA, every service reports healthy without operator action.
2. A failed gate prints the service name and its last health output.

distractors.name: Rotate Docker container logs on every guest
distractors.description:
## Problem

The `json-file` log driver kept every container log without a size limit. The `app` log on `tack-qa` grew to 14 GiB and filled the root volume.

## Change

Set `log-opts` with `max-size: 50m` and `max-file: 5` in `/etc/docker/daemon.json` through the Configs role. The change takes effect for new containers.

## Acceptance

1. `docker inspect` shows the log options on every recreated container.
2. The root volume on `tack-qa` stays below 70 percent after a week of soak traffic.

distractors.name: Upgrade Docker Engine on the data guests
distractors.description:
## Problem

The data guests run Docker Engine 27.5. Docker 28 fixes the routed IPv6 gateway mode that the compose network uses.

## Change

Update the apt pin in the Configs Docker role to 28.4. Upgrade QA first, then production during an approved window.

## Acceptance

1. `docker version` reports 28.4 on every data guest.
2. The routed bridge keeps its IPv6 gateway after the upgrade.

distractors.name: Stop the stack before restoring a volume snapshot
distractors.description:
## Problem

The recovery runbook restored a ZFS snapshot of the `tack_fdb-data` volume while the `fdb` container still ran. The store process wrote to files that the restore replaced, and the restored cluster reported corrupt pages.

## Change

The runbook stops every compose service on the guest with `docker compose down`, restores the snapshot, and starts the services again. The restore command refuses to run while a running container mounts the volume.

## Acceptance

1. A QA restore with the stack running fails with an explicit message.
2. A restore after `docker compose down` passes `fdbcli --exec status`.

distractors.name: Preserve Kafka consumer offsets across broker restarts
distractors.description:
## Problem

The single Kafka broker stored `__consumer_offsets` with a replication factor of one on an anonymous volume. A recreated broker container lost the offsets, and the audit consumer read the topic again from the start.

## Change

The broker uses the named volume `tack_kafka-data`. `ops audit consumer-offsets` prints the committed offset for each partition.

## Acceptance

1. A recreated broker keeps every committed offset.
2. The consumer resumes at the committed offsets without duplicate ledger rows.

distractors.name: Report stuck search work in verification output
distractors.description:
## Problem

`ops search verify` reported excluded nodes but not work items that had retried for hours. Operators could not see that indexing had stalled for one organization.

## Change

Verification lists each work item above the reporting threshold with its node, generation, attempt count, and last error.

## Acceptance

1. A work item with repeated engine failures appears in `stuck_work_items`.
2. Verification omits the item after the item completes.

distractors.name: Compute query token weights once per search session
distractors.description:
## Problem

Each continuation page called the model again to compute query token weights. Repeated calls added latency and could change results between pages.

## Change

The session stores the token weight map from the first call in FoundationDB. Every continuation uses that map again.

## Acceptance

1. A complete traversal sends one predict request.
2. A replayed page returns the same results.

distractors.name: Drain sessions before retiring the previous index
distractors.description:
## Problem

A full replacement waited for every open search session on the previous index. Abandoned sessions kept the old index for the whole absolute deadline.

## Change

Retirement waits for the idle deadline of each session instead of the absolute deadline. Tests drain their cursors before the replacement retires the previous index.

## Acceptance

1. A replacement retires the previous index within one idle timeout after the last page.
2. A cursor on the retired index returns an explicit expired session error.

distractors.name: Load the ledger node certificates on each data guest
distractors.description:
## Problem

The ledger nodes ran without TLS. Clients connected with `sslmode=disable` across guests.

## Change

The deploy writes each node certificate under `TACK_LEDGER_CERTS_DIR` and sets `TACK_LEDGER_TLS_ENABLED=true`. Every DSN uses `sslmode=verify-full` with the certificate authority of the deploy.

## Acceptance

1. A client with the wrong authority fails to connect.
2. `ops ledger node-wait` passes on every data guest with TLS enabled.

distractors.name: Limit search worker memory on large nodes
distractors.description:
## Problem

The content reader renders a complete node before it splits pages. A node with a 40 MiB description used more memory than the worker container limit, and the kernel killed the process.

## Change

The worker rejects a node larger than its byte budget with an explicit exclusion reason. The verification output reports the node and its size.

## Acceptance

1. Verification output lists a node above the budget with its size.
2. The worker continues with other nodes after the rejection.

distractors.name: Schedule weekly Proxmox host updates
distractors.description:
## Problem

The Proxmox hosts received security updates only when someone remembered to run them. Two hosts were three kernel versions behind.

## Change

Add a weekly maintenance window to the Configs inventory. The playbook applies package updates on one host, checks that its guests start again, and records the kernel version.

## Acceptance

1. Every host reports the current kernel after the window.
2. The playbook stops before the next host when a guest fails to start again.

distractors.name: Show the container image digest in the deploy summary
distractors.description:
## Problem

The deploy summary printed the image tag but not the digest. Two deploys with the tag `latest` could run different images.

## Change

The summary prints the repository digest of the `tack-server` and `tack-audit-consumer` images for each guest.

## Acceptance

1. The summary lists one digest per image per guest.
2. `ops deploy verify` compares those digests with the running containers.
